Dear Medical Director,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair for my patient {{patient_name}}. The Clinical Compass™ Rotator Cuff Decision Support assessment yielded a recommendation of "[Rotator Cuff Repair Recommendation]" (Class of Recommendation [COR]) based on the 2019 AAOS Clinical Practice Guideline for Rotator Cuff Tears.

CLINICAL JUSTIFICATION:
• Patient presents with symptomatic full-thickness rotator cuff tear with significant pain and functional impairment
• MRI-confirmed full-thickness tear of the [supraspinatus / infraspinatus / subscapularis]
• Failure of ≥6 weeks of conservative therapy documented
• Tear size and patient factors favor surgical repair to prevent progression

DIAGNOSIS:
• Tear type: Full-thickness rotator cuff tear — [DESCRIBE: supraspinatus, infraspinatus, subscapularis involvement]
• Tear size: [SMALL <1cm / MEDIUM 1-3cm / LARGE 3-5cm / MASSIVE >5cm]
• Affected side: [Right / Left]
• Chronicity: [Acute / Chronic — DURATION of symptoms]
• Fatty infiltration (Goutallier grade): [0-4]
• Muscle atrophy: [Present / Absent]

CONSERVATIVE THERAPY DOCUMENTATION:

• Physical therapy / rotator cuff strengthening: [DURATION — minimum 6 weeks, OUTCOMES]
• NSAIDs / analgesic medications: [MEDICATIONS, DURATION, RESPONSE]
• Subacromial corticosteroid injections: [NUMBER, DATES, RESPONSE]
• Activity modification: [DETAILS]

IMAGING FINDINGS:
• MRI shoulder ({{letter_date}}): Full-thickness tear of [TENDON(S)], [SIZE] cm, [DESCRIBE — retraction, fatty infiltration, muscle atrophy, associated pathology]
• Tendon retraction: [DESCRIBE — to level of humeral head / glenoid]
• Additional findings: [DESCRIBE — AC joint arthritis, biceps pathology, labral tear if applicable]

FUNCTIONAL ASSESSMENT:
• ASES Score: [SCORE] (normal ≥70; severe impairment <50)
• DASH Score: [SCORE] (higher = more disability)
• VAS Pain Score: [SCORE]/10
• Active ROM: Forward flexion [DEGREES], Abduction [DEGREES], External rotation [DEGREES]
• Strength testing: [DESCRIBE — weakness with abduction, external rotation, lift-off test]

MEDICAL NECESSITY:
Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair is medically necessary for this patient based on:
1. MRI-confirmed full-thickness rotator cuff tear with significant functional impairment
2. Failure of ≥6 weeks of comprehensive conservative therapy
3. Risk of tear progression, fatty infiltration, and muscle atrophy without surgical repair
4. Patient age and activity level favor surgical repair for optimal long-term outcome
5. Meets AAOS Class [I/IIa] criteria per 2019 Clinical Practice Guideline

GUIDELINE SUPPORT:
The 2019 AAOS Clinical Practice Guideline for Rotator Cuff Tears recommends surgical repair for full-thickness tears with persistent symptoms after conservative management. Evidence demonstrates that early repair prevents tear progression and preserves muscle quality (Moosmayer et al., JBJS 2014). Surgical repair is superior to physical therapy alone at 2-year follow-up (Kuhn et al., JSES 2013).

Without surgical repair, this patient faces progressive tear enlargement, fatty infiltration, and irreversible muscle atrophy — all of which significantly worsen surgical outcomes and may render the tear irreparable.

I respectfully request immediate reconsideration and approval of prior authorization for Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair (CPT 29827). Please contact my office at {{practice_phone}} or {{practice_email}} if additional clinical documentation is required.
